The draft anticipates exactly this and instructs 'If a cited file moves, re-measure.' I re-measured.

That statement remains true after the move because it is a statement about the pinned bytes, which I verified. Had it been phrased as a bare present-tense claim about D-103's adoption status, the move would have falsified it and I would be reporting this at a higher severity.

advisories.title: The COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin has stranded since the draft froze, and the D104-SF-1 rationale now describes a state the live register has moved past
advisories.detail: Two aspects of one event. First, the pin: the draft cites 12d192f7... and the live file is eddeb7c6.... Nothing the pin supports is falsified - I verified the move is additive and that all six decisions the draft relies on are byte-identical - but a turn-3 adoption entry that still carried 12d192f7... would be pinning a superseded register state, so the pin should be refreshed when this lands. Second, the rationale: the Alternatives entry rejects citing D-103 because it 'is not an adopted COORD entry at the pinned digest'. That remains true of the pinned bytes, and the qualifier is what keeps it true. But at the live head D-103 is adopted, so a reader measuring today will find the register and the rationale describing different worlds. A one-line turn-3 note - either citing D-103 now that it is adopted, or recording the deliberate choice to keep the precedent list to decisions adopted before this draft froze - would close the gap without changing any outcome.
advisories.severityNote: Advisory rather than SHOULD-FIX because the draft's own re-measure instruction covers the case, the qualifier makes the rationale survive, and I confirmed by block diff that no relied-upon content changed.

advisories.title: The precedent list groups D-013 and D-015 with D-035 and D-042 although the first two carried a file-08 row edit this decision declines, and the Measured inputs column headed 'Path' holds labels
advisories.detail: Two carried-forward citation-precision notes, both identical to what I raised on the D-103 draft, repeated here for consistency rather than as new defects. First: D-013's decision states 'the register row carries the acceptance. The row edit is this decision's only effect', and D-015 records the same wording class with its companion row, while D-035, D-042 and this draft carry the recording in the decisions file and explicitly do not edit file 08. So on the row-edit axis the four precedents split two and two. This is established practice - D-096, adopted at 0 MUST-FIX / 0 SHOULD-FIX from both reviewers, cites 'Same class as D-013 / D-035 / D-042 / D-066' while itself declining the file-08 edit - so it is not a defect this draft introduces, and the operative clauses state precisely what the decision does. Second: the Measured inputs table's first column is headed 'Path' but holds labels and bare filenames ('Claude 2 verdict', 'Codex verdict', 'file 08'); all seven entries resolved unambiguously by digest, but repository-relative paths would make the table self-resolving.
advisories.notBlocking: Every operative clause verified accurate; every cited digest resolved to exactly one live file.
